rationale: A wins because it treats missing proof as a landmine, not a copywriting opportunity. Its regulatory angle says, "This angle only works if you can answer the supply question on record," which is exactly the hard gate here. B has strong bones, but "branded drugmakers want it stopped" and "Patients priced out of branded weight-loss drugs" turn supplied facts into unsupported drama.
gaps_in_A: "The launch is a material event for a public company" gets ahead of the facts; public-company status does not automatically make this launch material.
"right after the profitability turn" leans on "recently" without a quarter or date. It asks for that proof later, but the why-now line should not outrun it.

"Patients priced out of branded semaglutide finally have an option" is refused correctly as written, but A could have preserved a narrower consumer access-and-risk angle if price and a real patient can be supplied.
gaps_in_B: "branded drugmakers want it stopped" overstates the update. The facts say manufacturers pushed back, not that they are trying to stop this specific Hims launch.
"The conflict exists today, not hypothetically" treats undated manufacturer pushback as a live peg. That is how you manufacture urgency and then get caught.
"Patients priced out of branded weight-loss drugs" invents the patient condition. Cheaper than branded drugs is not the same as documented patients being priced out.
"wagering its next growth chapter" is investor-story perfume. The update says Hims recently turned profitable and is launching this product; it does not say forward growth depends on it.
